title: Skills Banking and Hiring Forecast Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook standardizes how Redwood forecasts headcount needs and maintains a living "skills bank" of internal talent and stretch-ready candidates to reduce time-to-fill, improve role fit, and optimize hiring spend. The playbook covers quarterly forecast rhythms, the skills bank data model and maintenance, intake templates, approval gates, and post-hire follow-up that ties into performance and onboarding cycles.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time and long-term contractor hiring requests across engineering, product, and GTM functions.
- Does not replace team-level hiring approvals but provides a single canonical forecast and a prioritized queue for DRIs (directly responsible individuals).

Goals
- Reduce external hiring time-to-fill by 25% within 12 months by improving internal match rates and forecast accuracy.
- Increase internal mobility fills to 18% of total hires for roles that map cleanly to existing job families.
- Provide finance and recruiting with a rolling 6-quarter demand forecast and a 12-month skills hedge.

Definitions
- Skills Bank: A searchable inventory of internal employees and alumni who have recorded skill tags, stretch readiness, and availability windows.
- Hiring Forecast: A rolling forecast document (quarterly) of open roles, expected start windows, impact priority, and budget posture.
- Role Readiness Level (RRL): A 1–5 scale indicating how close an internal candidate is to performing at target for the role (1 = no overlap, 5 = ready to transition).

Ownership and Roles
- People Ops (Forecast Owner): Maintains the forecast cadence and publishes the rolling document.
- Hiring Manager (Requester): Completes intake, defines success metrics and ramp timeline.
- Recruiting: Provides time-to-fill estimates and sourcing plans; updates status in the queue.
- Finance: Signs off on budget exposure per quarter for committed hires.
- Mobility Panel (ad hoc): Reviews internal matches and recommends stretch assignments.

Quarterly Forecast Rhythm (Canonical Process)
1. Forecast Kickoff (weeks 1–2 of quarter)
   - Hiring managers submit role intents using the intake template (see below).
   - People Ops consolidates inputs and publishes a draft forecast to the leadership channel.
2. Prioritization Workshop (week 2)
   - Panel: People Ops, Recruiting Lead, Finance, 2 product/eng reps.
   - Output: Prioritized roster (A/B/C) and recommended hiring quarters.
3. Budget Gate (week 3)
   - Finance confirms budget for A and prioritized B items; unapproved items moved to the next quarter or paused.
4. Source Planning (week 3–4)
   - Recruiting assigns sourcers for approved items; internal mobility candidates pulled from Skills Bank first.
5. Execution & Rolling Review
   - Status updated weekly; forecast re-run mid-quarter if >20% change in committed headcount.

Intake Template (required fields)
| Field | Guidance |
| Role Title | Nominal title aligned to job family |
| Team | Team name and manager |
| Impact Priority (A/B/C) | A = mission critical this quarter |
| Target Start Quarter | e.g., Q4 2026 |
| Minimum Qualifications | Must-have skills |
| Preferred Qualifications | Nice-to-have or stretch skills |
| Ramp Metric | Specific metric for 90-day success (e.g., feature delivery, infra onboarding task) |
| Budget Code | Finance cost center |
| Internal Match Allowed | yes/no |

Approval Workflow (summary)
1. Hiring manager completes intake in People Ops form.
2. Recruiting validates time-to-fill and suggests sourcing mix.
3. Prioritization workshop assigns queue position.
4. Finance signs budget gate for A/B items.
5. Recruiting posts role; internal mobility candidates notified.

Skills Bank: Data Model and Maintenance
- Core attributes: employee_id, name, primary_team, job_family, skill_tags (list), RRL (1–5), last_updated, availability_window, coach/mentor, preferred_location.
- Ownership: Each manager confirms their team members' skills quarterly. People Ops performs a verification sweep during performance cycles.
- Update triggers: role change, end of project, 6-month cadence, or when an employee expresses mobility interest.

Search & Match Rules
- Exact match: RRL >= 4 and skill_tags cover >= 80% of required tags.
- Stretch match: RRL 2–3 with recorded mentor and 60–80% tag overlap; requires a 30–60 day development plan before start.
- Disqualification: RRL 1 or gaps in fundamental certifications for regulated roles (e.g., SOC/PDC-required).

Example Skills Bank JSON record (for Recruiting/Engineering tools)
{
  "employee_id": "E-11472",
  "name": "Nguyen Tran",
  "primary_team": "serving-runtime",
  "job_family": "infra_engineering",
  "skill_tags": ["CUDA","kernel-opt","python","profiling"],
  "RRL": "4",
  "last_updated": "2025-11-02",
  "availability_window": "Q1 2026",
  "coach": "Samira Ortiz"
}

Note: The above object is a canonical snippet; actual Skills Bank is stored in the HRIS + People Ops managed DB. Recruiting tools will sync a read-only subset nightly.

Internal Mobility Process
- Notification: When a role is posted, People Ops sends a digest to employees who match tags and have RRL >= 2.
- Mobility Panel Review: For RRL 2–3, a 30-minute panel (manager, receiving manager, mobility rep) sets a development plan and timeline.
- Transition Options: 1) Immediate transfer (RRL 4–5) with 2-week cross-training; 2) Stretch assignment (RRL 2–3) with 30–60 day upskilling and conditional transfer; 3) Mentored trial (part-time) for critical hires.

Onboarding & Post-Hire Linkage
- Each forecasted hire must define a 30/60/90 success plan at offer acceptance time. That plan becomes part of the onboarding checklist and the first manager 1:1 agenda items.
- Recruit-to-onboard handoff checklist (required to mark role as "Started"):
  - Offer accepted and paperwork complete
  - Cost center assigned and payroll initiated
  - New hire 30/60/90 plan uploaded to People Ops portal
  - Assigned mentor identified and calendar invites sent
  - Access list and critical systems provisioning requested (see Security handoff)

Metrics and Reporting (examples)
- Forecast accuracy: % of hires that start in the quarter they were forecasted. Target: 85%.
- Internal fill rate: % of roles filled by internal candidates. Target: 18%.
- Average time-to-fill for A-priority roles: target < 35 days.
- Skills Bank freshness: % of records updated in the last 180 days. Target: 90%.

Audit, Compliance and Data Handling
- Skills Bank contains personal data; retention and access follow the Data Management policy. Access limited to People Ops, Recruiting, managers, and authorized mobility panel members.
- Quarterly audit: People Ops runs a permissions report and an accuracy sample (20% of records) and publishes a short remediation report.

Manager Checklist (for hiring managers)
- Complete intake with clear success metrics.
- Confirm internal matches and discuss with Mobility Panel before external posting.
- Define ramp goals and 30/60/90 success signals at offer.
- Participate in the prioritization workshop and provide timely clarifications.

Playbook Exceptions and Edge Cases
- Emergency hires (business-critical, <14 days to fill) can bypass normal prioritization but must be ratified by VP People Ops and Finance within one week of start.
- Regulated roles requiring background certifications (legal/security) will have an additional compliance gate and a dedicated audit trail.

Change Log
- 2025-08-15: Initial draft and pilot with infra and product organizations.
- 2025-11-02: Skills Bank schema updated; added RRL definitions and stretch-match rules.
- 2026-01-20: Published playbook; targets and metrics added.
